mainTopic: ירבעם's sins, his rise and refusal to repent, and the lasting effect of the golden calf
overview: The גמרא continues the story of ירבעם. Even the נביא אחיה השילוני signed on to ירבעם's rule, and the גמרא brings פסוקים showing that the righteous king יהוא still kept ירבעם's sins. אביי and רבא give two reasons why: אביי blames יהוא's own words, and רבא blames אחיה's signature. רבי יוחנן teaches that ירבעם's people threatened death to anyone who went up to ירושלים for the רגל. The גמרא then explains the פסוק of ירבעם meeting אחיה השילוני. It brings רבי יוסי's teaching about times and places set aside for disaster, and it praises ירבעם's early greatness in תורה. רבי חנינא בר פפא teaches that enjoying the world without a ברכה is like robbing ה׳ and כנסת ישראל, which makes a person a partner of ירבעם. The גמרא then discusses the golden calf and how its punishment lasts for generations. Finally, ירבעם refuses ה׳'s offer of תשובה because דוד would walk ahead of him, and a story about רבי אבהו begins that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Even אחיה השילוני made a mistake and signed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that even the נביא אחיה השילוני erred and signed on to ירבעם's arrangement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even אחיה השילוני made a mistake and signed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that even a great נביא, אחיה השילוני, wrongly signed his name in support of ירבעם. This sets up the next step, which shows how much harm that signature did later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is surprising because אחיה השילוני was the נביא who first told ירבעם he would become king. The claim here is that his signature gave ירבעם's path a stamp of approval that later generations would rely on.

keyTerms.meaning: Achiya from Shilo, the נביא who told ירבעם he would rule

phrases.english: And even Achiya the Shilonite
erred and signed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of ירבעם's rule and those who signed on to it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even אחיה השילוני wrongly signed in support of ירבעם.

steps.title: Proof: righteous יהוא still followed ירבעם's sins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the damage of that signature: יהוא was very righteous, as one פסוק says, yet another פסוק says he did not turn away from ירבעם's sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: For יהוא was a very righteous man, as it says: 'And ה׳ said to יהוא: Because you did well in doing what is right in My eyes, and did to the house of אחאב everything that was in My heart, your descendants to the fourth generation will sit on the throne of ישראל.' And it is written: 'But יהוא did not take care to walk in the תורה of ה׳, God of ישראל, with all his heart. He did not turn away from the sins of ירבעם, who caused ישראל to sin.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two פסוקים about יהוא. One shows that God praised him greatly, and the next shows that he still kept ירבעם's sinful practices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If יהוא was so righteous, how could he keep ירבעם's sins? The two פסוקים create a puzzle, and the next steps give two explanations. אביי blames יהוא's own words, and רבא blames אחיה השילוני's signature.

keyTerms.meaning: king of ישראל who wiped out the house of אחאב
the family and dynasty of king אחאב
the sins of ירבעם, meaning his golden calves

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two פסוקים. The first one praises יהוא, and the second one criticizes him. The whole point is that both are true about the same man.

phrases.english: For Yehu was a very righteous man,
as it is stated: 'And ה׳ said to Yehu:
Because you have done well
to do what is right in My eyes,
according to all that was in My heart
you have done to the house of Achav,
your children of the fourth generation will sit
on the throne of Israel.'
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 10:30

phrases.english: And it is written: 'But Yehu did not take care
to walk in the Torah of ה׳, God of Israel,
with all his heart;
he did not turn away from the sins of Yeravam
who caused Israel to sin.'
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 10:31

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what came of אחיה השילוני's signature.
steps.raayaObject: That יהוא, a great צדיק, still kept ירבעם's sins, which needs an explanation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב 10:30-31: יהוא is praised as righteous yet keeps ירבעם's sins.

steps.title: What made Yehu sin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what caused a righteous man like יהוא to follow ירבעם's sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: What caused him to do this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question: what made יהוא go wrong? This sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים seem to clash, since a great צדיק would not be expected to keep idol worship going. The גמרא wants to know what pushed him into it.

phrases.english: What caused him to do this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the clash in the two פסוקים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What caused the righteous יהוא to keep ירבעם's sins.

steps.title: אביי: words spoken out loud have power
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that a covenant is made with the lips. יהוא said he would serve the בעל much, and that statement drew him toward doing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: A covenant is made with the lips, as it says: 'אחאב served the בעל a little; יהוא will serve him much.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the first answer. יהוא once said, as a trick, that he would serve the בעל a lot, and those words had an effect on him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהוא said this to trap the worshippers of the בעל, not because he meant it. אביי teaches that even words said without meaning them can pull a person toward what he said.

keyTerms.meaning: a covenant is made with the lips; spoken words have power

phrases.english: Abaye said: A covenant is made with the lips,
as it is stated: 'Achav served the Baal a little,
Yehu will serve him much.'
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 10:18. יהוא said this as a trick to gather the בעל's worshippers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יהוא's own words, said as a trick, pulled him toward idol worship.

steps.title: רבא: יהוא saw אחיה's signature and was misled
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that יהוא saw אחיה השילוני's signature and wrongly thought ירבעם's ways were allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: He saw the seal of אחיה השילוני, and he made a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer to the same question. יהוא saw the signature of the great נביא אחיה השילוני and thought ירבעם's path must be acceptable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's answer ties straight back to step 1, where we learned that אחיה signed. The error of one great person became the reason another great person went wrong.
steps.whatToRemember: Two reasons are given for why יהוא sinned. אביי says his own words drew him in, and רבא says אחיה השילוני's signature misled him.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how much responsibility a leader carries. A mistaken approval from a great person can mislead people generations later.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: חוֹתָמוֹ שֶׁל אֲחִיָּה הַשִּׁילוֹנִי
phrases.english: Rava said: The seal of Achiya the Shilonite
he saw, and he erred.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: חוֹתָמוֹ שֶׁל אֲחִיָּה הַשִּׁילוֹנִי רָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer from אביי's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יהוא was misled by אחיה השילוני's signature on ירבעם's rule.

steps.title: Yeravam's decree was harsher than God's command
steps.stepSummary: On a פסוק in הושע, רבי יוחנן teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא said: I made not going up for the רגל a broken מצות עשה, but they made going up a crime punished by the sword.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And the rebels have gone deep in slaughter, and I am rejected by them all.' רבי יוחנן said: הקדוש ברוך הוא said: They went deeper than I did. I said: Anyone who does not go up for the רגל breaks a מצות עשה. And they said: Anyone who goes up for the רגל will be stabbed with the sword.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new teaching about ירבעם. רבי יוחנן explains a פסוק to show that ירבעם's people made a harsher law against going to ירושלים than God's law requiring it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: God's punishment for skipping עלייה לרגל is only that you broke a מצות עשה. ירבעם's people threatened death for going. Their law was stricter than God's, and that is how they kept people away from ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: they went deep, they went further
going up to ירושלים for a festival
will be stabbed with the sword

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And the rebels have gone deep in slaughter,
and I am rejected by them all.'
phrases.notes: הושע 5:2

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
They went deeper than Mine.
phrases.notes: In other words, their decree was more extreme than God's own rule.

phrases.aramaic: אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ עוֹלֶה לָרֶגֶל
phrases.english: I said: Anyone who does not go up for the festival
breaks a positive commandment,
and they said: Anyone who goes up for the festival
will be stabbed with the sword.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching about ירבעם's reign.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ירבעם's people made going up for the רגל punishable by death, which was harsher than God's command to go.

steps.title: 'At that time' means a time set aside for disaster
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק of ירבעם meeting אחיה השילוני, and a ברייתא in the name of רבי יוסי teaches that 'at that time' signals a time prepared for trouble.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And it was at that time, when ירבעם went out of ירושלים, that אחיה השילוני the נביא found him on the road, and he was wearing a new garment.' It was taught in the name of רבי יוסי: It was a time set aside for disaster.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining a new פסוק about ירבעם's first meeting with אחיה השילוני. רבי יוסי teaches that the words 'at that time' point to a time meant for disaster.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra words 'at that time' are read as a hint. This meeting began ירבעם's rise, which would bring great trouble on ישראל, so the time itself was marked for disaster.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught, introducing a ברייתא

phrases.english: 'And it came to pass at that time,
and Yeravam went out of Jerusalem,

phrases.aramaic: וַיִּמְצָא אֹתוֹ אֲחִיָּה הַשִּׁילוֹנִי הַנָּבִיא בַּדֶּרֶךְ
phrases.english: and Achiya the Shilonite, the prophet, found him on the road,
and he was clothed in a new garment.'
phrases.notes: מלכים א 11:29

phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Yosei:
It is a time set aside for disaster.
phrases.notes: He is explaining the words 'at that time' from the פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining a new פסוק about ירבעם and אחיה השילוני.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The phrase 'at that time' marks a time set aside for disaster.

steps.title: More times set aside for trouble, and one set aside for good
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי reads four more פסוקים about 'time.' Three show a time set aside for trouble, and one shows a time set aside for good.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'At the time of their punishment they shall perish': רבי יוסי taught that this is a time set aside for trouble. 'In a time of favor I answered you': a time set aside for good. 'On the day I punish, I will punish their sin upon them': a time set aside for trouble. 'And it was at that time, and יהודה went down from his brothers': a time set aside for trouble.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the list started in the last step. It brings more פסוקים where רבי יוסי says a 'time' was specially set aside, usually for trouble but once for good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 used this rule on the meeting of ירבעם and אחיה. Here the גמרא shows it is a general pattern of רבי יוסי across תנ״ך. The 'time of favor' example shows the idea works both ways: some times are set aside for good.

keyTerms.meaning: A time that is set aside or prepared in advance
A time of favor, when prayers are accepted

phrases.english: "At the time of their punishment, they shall perish,"
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 51:18

phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Yosei:
A time set aside for trouble.
"In a time of favor I answered you,"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 49:8

phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Yosei:
A time set aside for good.
"And on the day I punish, I will punish their sin upon them,"
phrases.notes: שמות 32:34

phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Yosei:
It is a time set aside for trouble.
"And it was at that time
and Judah went down from his brothers,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 38:1

phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Yosei:
A time set aside for trouble.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of רבי יוסי's teachings begun in step 7 with more examples.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a פסוק stresses a particular 'time', רבי יוסי reads it as a time set aside, usually for trouble and sometimes for good.

steps.title: שכם is a place set aside for trouble
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי teaches that שכם is a place set aside for trouble, and lists three bad events that happened there.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And רחבעם went to שכם, for all Israel came to שכם to make him king': רבי יוסי taught that it is a place set aside for trouble. In שכם they harmed דינה, in שכם the brothers sold יוסף, and in שכם the kingdom of דוד's family was split.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי takes his idea from time and applies it to a place. He says שכם is a place set aside for trouble and proves it with three events.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the pattern was about times. Now it is about a place. The splitting of דוד's kingdom in the days of רחבעם and ירבעם fits into a longer history of bad things at שכם.

keyTerms.meaning: A place set aside or prepared in advance
A city in the land of Israel, the place where the kingdom split
The kingdom of דוד's family was split

phrases.english: "And Rehoboam went to Shechem,
for to Shechem all Israel came
to make him king."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 12:1

phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Yosei:
A place set aside for trouble.
In Shechem they harmed Dinah,
in Shechem his brothers sold Joseph,
in Shechem the kingdom of the house of David was split.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מָקוֹם מְזוּמָּן לְפוּרְעָנוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבי יוסי's pattern from times to a place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שכם is a place set aside for trouble, as shown by three bad events that happened there.

steps.title: ירבעם left Jerusalem's destiny
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר פפא reads 'ירבעם went out from Jerusalem' as meaning he cut himself off from Jerusalem's lot.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And ירבעם went out from Jerusalem': רבי חנינא בר פפא said this means he went out from the lot (destiny) of Jerusalem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story of ירבעם and explains one more phrase from the פסוק. It says he did not just leave the city; he left Jerusalem's destiny.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the פסוק only says ירבעם physically left the city. רבי חנינא בר פפא reads it as a spiritual break: ירבעם removed himself from Jerusalem's share for good.

keyTerms.meaning: A slip or note; here, the lot or destiny of a place
An אמורא who explains this פסוק

phrases.english: "And Jeroboam went out from Jerusalem,"
phrases.notes: מלכים א 11:29

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa said:
That he went out from the destiny of Jerusalem.
phrases.notes: Literally 'from Jerusalem's slip of paper.' He cut himself off from the share of the people of Jerusalem.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא: שֶׁיָּצָא מִפִּיתְקָהּ שֶׁל יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from רבי יוסי's list to explaining the פסוקים about ירבעם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Went out from Jerusalem' means ירבעם left Jerusalem's destiny for good.

steps.title: What does 'a new garment' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק of אחיה finding ירבעם in a new garment and asks what 'new garment' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And אחיה השילוני the prophet found him on the way, and he was wearing a new garment, and the two of them were alone in the field.' What is meant by 'in a new garment'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the פסוק and asks about the odd detail of the 'new garment.' This sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would the פסוק bother telling us what someone was wearing? The גמרא assumes the detail must teach something, so it asks.

keyTerms.meaning: The prophet who told ירבעם he would rule

phrases.english: "And the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him on the way,
and he was covered in a new garment,
and the two of them were alone in the field."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 11:29

phrases.english: What is meant by "in a new garment"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the same ירבעם פסוק, now asking about a specific detail.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson is taught by the detail that he wore a 'new garment'?

steps.title: ירבעם's Torah was flawless like a new garment
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן reads it as 'like a new garment': just as a new garment has no flaw, ירבעם's Torah learning had no flaw.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: like a new garment. Just as a new garment has no flaw, so too the Torah of ירבעם had no flaw.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question. The garment is a picture of ירבעם's Torah, which was perfect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן reads 'in a new garment' as 'like a new garment,' so the garment becomes a comparison. The point is that ירבעם was a flawless Torah scholar at that time, which makes his later fall more striking.

keyTerms.meaning: His Torah, meaning his Torah learning

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
Like a new garment.
phrases.notes: He reads the letter ב ('in') as if it were כ ('like'), turning it into a comparison.

phrases.aramaic: מָה שַׂלְמָה חֲדָשָׁה אֵין בָּהּ שׁוּם דּוֹפִי –
phrases.english: Just as a new garment has no flaw at all,
so too the Torah of Jeroboam
had no flaw at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The new garment stands for ירבעם's Torah, which had no flaw.

steps.title: They came up with brand-new Torah ideas
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation: 'new garment' means they came up with new ideas that no ear had ever heard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'a new garment' means that they came up with new ideas that no ear had ever heard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the question about the 'new garment.' Here 'new' means new Torah ideas.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer focused on 'garment' as a picture of something without flaws. This answer focuses on the word 'new' (חדשה), linking it to חידשו, 'they came up with new things.'

keyTerms.meaning: They came up with something new
That no ear had ever heard

steps.whatToRemember: ירבעם began as a great Torah scholar, perfect in his learning and full of new ideas. This makes his later sins, which the גמרא is discussing, even more tragic.

phrases.english: Another explanation: "a new garment" means
that they came up with new ideas
phrases.notes: 'They' fits the two people in the פסוק, ירבעם and אחיה, alone together.

phrases.english: that no ear had ever heard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different answer to the question in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'New garment' means they came up with Torah ideas never heard before.

steps.title: What does 'the two were alone in the field' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the end of the פסוק about אחיה and ירבעם means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'and the two of them were alone in the field'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the same פסוק about אחיה and ירבעם and asks what they come to teach. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying they were 'alone in a field' sounds like a plain detail of the story. The גמרא assumes the words carry a lesson about how great these two men were. That is why it asks.

keyTerms.meaning: Alone, just the two of them

phrases.english: What is 'and the two of them were alone in the field'?
phrases.notes: מלכים א 11:29, the same פסוק as the 'new garment'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same פסוק, now its last words.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson is hidden in the words 'alone in the field'.

steps.title: Everyone else was like grass next to them
steps.stepSummary: רב says that compared to them, all other תלמידי חכמים seemed like grass of the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: it means that all the Torah scholars seemed, next to them, like the grass of the field.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that 'alone' means nobody else counted next to them. Other scholars were like grass compared to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Alone' does not mean that no other people existed. It means no one else was on their level. The word 'field' is used for the picture: the others were like low grass, and the two of them stood tall.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
That all the Torah scholars
seemed, before them, like the grass of the field.
phrases.notes: 'Before them' means compared to אחיה and ירבעם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Alone' means unmatched. Other scholars were like grass next to them.

steps.title: The Torah's reasons were open to them like a field
steps.stepSummary: A second view says that all the Torah's reasons were as open to them as an open field.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: it means that all the reasons of the Torah were revealed to them like an open field.
steps.whatsHappening: A second explanation is given. Here the 'field' is a picture of how openly they understood the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first answer, the field is about the other scholars, who were like grass. In this answer, the field is about the Torah itself, which lay wide open to them. This matches step 13, where the 'new garment' was explained as their new Torah ideas.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
That all the reasons of the Torah
were revealed to them like a field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'field' shows that the Torah's reasons were wide open to them.

steps.title: A בת קול rebukes the people for sending away דוד's sons
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר פפא reads a פסוק in מיכה as a בת קול scolding the people for rejecting the family of דוד, the one who won them גת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Therefore you will give parting gifts to מורשת גת; the houses of אכזיב will be a letdown to the kings of ישראל.' רבי חנינא בר פפא said: a בת קול came out and said to them: 'The one who killed the Philistine and gave you גת to inherit, will you give parting gifts to his sons?' In the end, 'the houses of אכזיב will be a letdown to the kings of ישראל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק, and רבי חנינא בר פפא explains it as a heavenly voice scolding the people. They were sending away the sons of דוד, even though דוד had won them the city of גת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Giving parting gifts' is read as saying goodbye to דוד's family. In this sugya, that means leaving them to follow ירבעם. The end of the פסוק is a warning: the new kings of Israel will let the people down, the way a dried-up stream disappoints (אכזב means disappointing).

phrases.english: 'Therefore you will give parting gifts over Moreshes Gath;
phrases.notes: מיכה 1:14

phrases.english: the houses of Achziv will be a letdown to the kings of Israel.'
Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa said:
A heavenly voice came out and said to them:
The one who killed the Philistine
phrases.notes: This is דוד, who killed גלית.

phrases.english: and gave you Gath as an inheritance,
will you give parting gifts to his sons?
'The houses of Achziv will be a letdown to the kings of Israel.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לָכֵן תִּתְּנִי שִׁלּוּחִים עַל מוֹרֶשֶׁת גַּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching from רבי חנינא בר פפא about the split under ירבעם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people were wrong to send away דוד's sons, and the kings of Israel would end up disappointing them.

steps.title: Enjoying without a ברכה is like stealing
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר פפא teaches that someone who enjoys this world without a ברכה is like a person robbing הקדוש ברוך הוא and כנסת ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר פפא said: anyone who enjoys something from this world without a ברכה is as if he robs הקדוש ברוך הוא and כנסת ישראל. As the פסוק says: 'One who robs his father and his mother and says it is no sin is a companion to a destroyer.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא בר פפא gives a new teaching: taking pleasure from the world without a ברכה is a kind of robbery. He brings a פסוק in משלי as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The world belongs to ה׳, and the ברכה is what allows us to enjoy it. Skipping the ברכה is like taking without permission. The פסוק speaks of robbing a 'father and mother', and the next step will explain who they are.

keyTerms.meaning: The Jewish people as a whole

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous source for how serious it is to say a ברכה before enjoying food or anything else.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa said:
Anyone who enjoys something from this world
without a blessing,
it is as if he robs the Holy One, Blessed be He
and the congregation of Israel,
as it says: 'One who robs his father and his mother'
phrases.notes: משלי 28:24

phrases.english: and says, 'It is no sin',
is a companion to a man who destroys.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא: כׇּל הַנֶּהֱנֶה מִן הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּלֹא בְּרָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching from the same רבי חנינא בר פפא, which will connect back to ירבעם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Enjoying this world without a ברכה is like robbing הקדוש ברוך הוא and כנסת ישראל.

steps.title: Proving who the 'father' and 'mother' are
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר פפא proves from other פסוקים that 'father' means הקדוש ברוך הוא and 'mother' means כנסת ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'His father' can only mean הקדוש ברוך הוא, as it says: 'Is He not your father who made you?' And 'his mother' can only mean כנסת ישראל, as it says: 'Hear, my son, the discipline of your father, and do not abandon the Torah of your mother.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא בר פפא backs up his teaching. He uses two פסוקים to show who the 'father' and 'mother' in the robbery פסוק really are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this proof, the פסוק would sound like it is about robbing your own parents. The פסוק in דברים calls ה׳ our father. The פסוק in משלי speaks of the 'Torah of your mother', meaning the tradition kept by the Jewish people. So the robbery is from ה׳ and from כנסת ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Who made you, who acquired you

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין אָבִיו אֶלָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: And 'his father' means none other than the Holy One, Blessed be He,
as it says: 'Is He not your father who made you?'
phrases.notes: דברים 32:6

phrases.english: And 'his mother' means none other than the congregation of Israel,
as it says: 'Hear, my son, the discipline of your father,'
phrases.notes: משלי 1:8

phrases.english: 'and do not abandon the Torah of your mother.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין אָבִיו אֶלָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the teaching in step 18 by explaining its פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That 'father and mother' in משלי 28:24 means הקדוש ברוך הוא and כנסת ישראל.

steps.title: Who is the 'destroyer'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'a companion to a destroyer' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'he is a companion to a man who destroys'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the last words of the robbery פסוק: who is this 'destroyer'? This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father and mother have already been explained. Now the גמרא wants to know which specific destroyer the פסוק means.

phrases.english: What is 'he is a companion to a man who destroys'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the final words of the פסוק quoted in step 18.

steps.title: The destroyer is ירבעם בן נבט
steps.stepSummary: The 'destroyer' is ירבעם בן נבט, who ruined the bond between Israel and their Father in Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is a companion of ירבעם בן נבט, who corrupted Israel before their Father in Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the destroyer is ירבעם בן נבט. This brings the teaching back to the main subject of the sugya.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירבעם is called a destroyer because he led Israel away from ה׳. Someone who skips a ברכה also 'robs' that same Father. So he is put in the same group as ירבעם.

keyTerms.meaning: The first king of the northern kingdom, who led Israel to sin

steps.whatToRemember: Enjoying the world without a ברכה is like robbing ה׳ and כנסת ישראל. The person who does it is called a partner of ירבעם, who pulled Israel away from their Father in Heaven.

phrases.english: He is a companion of Jeroboam son of Nebat,
who corrupted Israel
before their Father in Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The destroyer is ירבעם בן נבט.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Skipping a ברכה puts a person in the same group as ירבעם, who corrupted Israel.

steps.title: ירבעם pushed Israel away like one stick knocking another
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנין explains the פסוק in מלכים ב that says ירבעם 'drove' Israel away from ה׳: it was like two sticks hitting each other and flying apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And ירבעם (son of נבט) drove Israel away from following ה׳ and caused them to sin a great sin.' רבי חנין said: It was like two sticks that knock each other away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק about ירבעם, and רבי חנין gives a picture of what 'drove away' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The step before called ירבעם a 'destroyer' who ruined Israel's bond with ה׳. Here רבי חנין shows how forceful that was: like one stick striking another and sending it flying. ירבעם did not just lead Israel a little off track; he knocked them far away from ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: and he drove away / pushed away
and he caused them to sin
that knock away, that send flying

phrases.english: "And Jeroboam (son of Nevat) drove
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some don't.

phrases.english: Israel away from following God,
and caused them to sin a great sin."
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 17:21

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanin said:
"Like two sticks
that knock each other away."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of ירבעם as the one who broke Israel's bond with ה׳, now explaining a פסוק about it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ירבעם's pushing Israel away from ה׳ was forceful, like one stick knocking another far away.

steps.title: משה blames the gold for the golden calf
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי reads the place name 'די זהב' in דברים as a hint: משה told ה׳ that the overflowing gold He gave Israel is what led them to make a golden god.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק mentions 'די זהב'. The school of רבי ינאי said: משה said to ה׳: Master of the world, the silver and gold You poured out on Israel, until they said 'Enough!', is what caused them to make gods of gold.
steps.whatsHappening: Since we were talking about ירבעם's calves, the גמרא now turns to the first calf, the golden calf in the desert, and shows how משה defended Israel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name 'די זהב' literally sounds like 'enough gold'. The school of רבי ינאי reads it as משה's argument: Israel had so much gold that they said 'Enough!', and that wealth led them into the sin. This partly shifts the blame away from Israel.

keyTerms.meaning: that You poured out in abundance

phrases.english: "And Di Zahav."
phrases.notes: דברים 1:1. It is a place name, but it literally sounds like 'enough gold'.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: Moshe said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world,
because of the silver and gold
that You poured out on Israel
until they said 'Enough!',
it caused them
to make for themselves gods of gold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from ירבעם's calves to the original golden calf in the desert.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה argued that the great wealth ה׳ gave Israel is what led them to make the golden calf.

steps.title: The parable of the lion and the basket of meat
steps.stepSummary: A parable backs up משה's argument: a lion only roars and attacks when it is over a basket of meat, not a basket of straw.
steps.simpleTranslation: A parable: A lion does not attack and roar over a basket of straw, but over a basket of meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a parable to support what משה said in the step before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lion gets wild and bold when it has rich food, not plain straw. In the same way, Israel became bold enough to sin because they were full and wealthy. This makes משה's argument easier to understand: the plenty itself stirred them up.

phrases.english: A parable:
A lion does not attack and roar
over a basket of straw,
but over a basket of meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports משה's argument with a picture from everyday life.
steps.raayaObject: משה's claim that wealth caused Israel to sin with the golden calf.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A parable: a lion roars over meat, not over straw.

steps.title: ירבעם added more calves to Israel's burden
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא says that until ירבעם, Israel suffered from one calf; after ירבעם, from two and three calves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: Until ירבעם, Israel was nursing from one calf. From then on, from two and three calves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא connects the golden calf in the desert to ירבעם's calves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Israel was already paying for the one golden calf from the desert. ירבעם set up two more calves, so now the punishment came from three calves together. This shows how much ירבעם added to Israel's sin.

keyTerms.meaning: nursing, drawing from (here: suffering the results of)

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said:
Until Jeroboam, Israel was
nursing from one calf;
phrases.notes: 'Nursing' here means feeling the results of a sin. The one calf is the golden calf in the desert.

phrases.english: from then on,
from two and three calves.
phrases.notes: ירבעם set up two calves, one in בית אל and one in דן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the golden calf just discussed back to ירבעם's calves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ירבעם's two calves added to the burden Israel already carried from the golden calf.

steps.title: Every punishment carries a tiny piece of the golden calf
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that every punishment that comes to the world includes a small piece of the punishment for the first calf.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: There is no punishment that comes to the world that does not include one twenty-fourth of the tipping-weight of a ליטרא of the first calf.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק makes a big claim about the golden calf; the next step will bring his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The golden calf was never fully paid off all at once. Instead, a tiny extra amount of its punishment is added to every later punishment. The picture of a small weight that tips the scale shows how small the added part is, yet it is always there.

keyTerms.meaning: the small extra weight that tips the scale
the first calf (the golden calf in the desert)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
There is no punishment at all
that comes to the world
that does not have in it one twenty-fourth
of the tipping-weight of a litra
phrases.notes: Picture a scale: the הכרע is the little extra that tips it. So he means a very small added amount.

phrases.english: of the first calf,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the lasting effect of the golden calf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A small portion of the golden calf's punishment is added to every punishment that comes to the world.

steps.title: Proof: ה׳ said He would punish the calf 'on the day I punish'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק proves his point from the פסוק in שמות where ה׳ says He will punish their sin on the day He punishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And on the day I punish, I will punish their sin upon them.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the proof for רבי יצחק's statement in the step before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ said this right after the golden calf. Instead of punishing it fully right away, He said He would bring it up 'on the day I punish', meaning whenever any punishment comes. That is why every punishment carries a piece of the calf.

keyTerms.meaning: my punishing, when I take account
and I will punish / bring to account

phrases.english: as it says:
"And on the day I punish,
I will punish their sin upon them."
phrases.notes: שמות 32:34

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק that supports רבי יצחק's statement.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יצחק's claim that every punishment includes part of the golden calf's punishment.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 32:34: 'And on the day I punish, I will punish their sin upon them.'

steps.title: The golden calf's debt was collected after twenty-four generations
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says the punishment promised in that פסוק was finally collected twenty-four generations later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: After twenty-four generations, this פסוק was collected.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא adds that the punishment for the golden calf was finally paid at a specific time; the next step brings his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק spoke of small pieces added over time. רבי חנינא adds that the payment promised in this פסוק came due after twenty-four generations. He treats the פסוק like a debt that was finally collected.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
After twenty-four generations
this verse was collected,
phrases.notes: Like a debt being paid: the punishment ה׳ promised in שמות 32:34 finally came.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the פסוק just quoted, saying when its punishment was finally collected.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The punishment promised for the golden calf was collected twenty-four generations later.

steps.title: Proof from יחזקאל: 'Those in charge of the city, draw near'
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא proves his point from יחזקאל, where those 'in charge' of the city are called to come with destroying weapons.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And he called in my ears with a loud voice, saying: Draw near, those in charge of the city, each man with his destroying weapon in his hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the proof for רבי חנינא's statement that the golden calf's debt was collected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word for 'those in charge' (פקודות) comes from the same root as 'I will punish' (פקדי) in the שמות פסוק. So רבי חנינא sees יחזקאל's vision of destruction as the day ה׳ finally 'punished' the sin of the calf. That vision came twenty-four generations after the calf.

keyTerms.meaning: those in charge of the city

steps.whatToRemember: The golden calf was not a one-time event. רבי אושעיא says ירבעם's calves added to it, רבי יצחק says a tiny piece of it is in every punishment, and רבי חנינא says its debt was collected in the time of יחזקאל, twenty-four generations later.

phrases.english: as it says:
"And he called in my ears with a loud voice, saying:
Draw near, those in charge of the city,
phrases.notes: פקודות shares its root with פקדי, 'I will punish', in the שמות פסוק. That is the link.

phrases.english: each man with his destroying weapon in his hand."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 9:1

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק that supports רבי חנינא's statement.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא's claim that the golden calf's punishment was collected after twenty-four generations.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 9:1, where the word פקודות echoes 'I will punish' from שמות 32:34.

steps.title: What does 'after this matter' refer to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק saying ירבעם did not turn back from his evil way 'after this matter' and asks what event 'after' is pointing to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'After this matter, ירבעם did not return from his evil way.' The גמרא asks: after what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about ירבעם and asks what the word 'after' is pointing to. This question sets up רבי אבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'after this matter' suggests that something specific happened that should have made ירבעם change. The גמרא wants to know what that event was. Knowing it shows how stubborn ירבעם really was.

keyTerms.meaning: Did not return, did not repent

phrases.english: "After this matter,
Jeroboam did not return from his evil way."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 13:33

phrases.english: What is meant by "after"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the punishment for the calves (steps 25-29) to a new פסוק about ירבעם's refusal to repent.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which event the word 'after' in the פסוק is pointing to.

steps.title: ה׳ offers ירבעם גן עדן, but ירבעם refuses to walk behind דוד
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא explains that ה׳ grabbed ירבעם by his garment and promised him a walk in גן עדן with דוד if he repented. ירבעם asked who would lead, heard it would be דוד, and refused.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: It was after ה׳ grabbed ירבעם by his garment and said, 'Repent, and you, I and the son of ישי will walk together in גן עדן.' ירבעם asked, 'Who will be in front?' ה׳ answered, 'The son of ישי will be in front.' ירבעם said, 'If so, I don't want it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא answers the question: 'after' means after ה׳ Himself begged ירבעם to repent, and ירבעם turned Him down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ offered ירבעם a huge reward, a place in גן עדן right next to Him. ירבעם gave it up because he could not stand being second to דוד. His pride was stronger than his wish to be close to ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: The son of ישי, meaning דוד המלך
We will stroll in גן עדן

steps.whatToRemember: ירבעם lost גן עדן through jealousy and pride. He refused to repent because דוד would walk ahead of him.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Grabbed him by his garment' is a picture of ה׳ pulling hard to bring ירבעם back. It is not about ירבעם's clothing.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why ירבעם is one of the kings with no share in the World-to-Come. He was given the chance to repent and chose not to.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
After the Holy One, Blessed be He, grabbed
Jeroboam by his garment,
and said to him: Repent,
and I, you, and the son of Yishai
phrases.notes: The son of ישי is דוד המלך.

phrases.english: will stroll in the Garden of Eden.
He said to Him: Who will be at the head?
The son of Yishai will be at the head.
phrases.notes: The text doesn't say who is talking here, but it's ה׳ answering ירבעם.

phrases.english: If so, I do not want it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: אַחַר שֶׁתְּפָשׂוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'After' refers to ה׳ begging ירבעם to repent and offering him גן עדן with דוד, an offer ירבעם turned down out of pride.

steps.title: רבי אבהו stops lecturing about the three kings after falling ill
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a story: רבי אבהו used to lecture about the three kings, fell ill, and took on himself to stop. The story continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו used to lecture about the three kings. He fell ill and promised himself not to lecture about them anymore. Once...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about רבי אבהו and his lectures on the three kings. The story is only starting here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו connected his illness to his lectures about these kings, so he promised to stop. The word 'once' signals that something is about to happen that will test his promise.

keyTerms.meaning: The three kings who have no share in the World-to-Come
He took upon himself, he promised

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu was accustomed
to lecture about the three kings.
phrases.notes: These are the three kings the משנה lists as having no share in the World-to-Come.

phrases.english: He fell ill,
and took upon himself that he would not lecture about them.
Once...
phrases.notes: The sentence breaks off here. The story picks up on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ הֲוָה רְגִיל דַּהֲוָה קָא דָרֵישׁ בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה מְלָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story about how the חכמים treated lectures on the three kings, moving on from the ירבעם story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אבהו stopped lecturing about the three kings after he fell ill. The story continues beyond this point.
